fields.statement: At 21c1eb26 I ran go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/api -run TestFlakyTestBugs -v (PASS, and PASS again with -count=3). It covers: one bug request for a newly flaky test naming the test, PR #7 and head aaa111 and asking to reproduce locally and fix or quarantine; no second request on a repeat poll or on a second flake of the same test while the first is open; TestB and TestAB each queued once; no request with fileBugs off. On attempt 1 the finding was that a planned request let the same flake be filed again. The new flakyBugFiled treats queued and planning requests as open. A planned or failed request covers the runs its text names and any flake recorded before its run finished, so only a later flake files the test again. The new test step plans request R1 through a finished journal, sees nothing queued over two polls, then sees exactly one new TestA request for the later flake ddd444. go vet and gofmt are clean on internal/api. A full go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/api ran every test with no --- FAIL. The package was failed only by the harness guard that the enclosing ~/code root's .rhiza-root/usage.live.json changed. That file is the live root daemon's and this diff (watchdog_flaky.go and its test) does not touch it. An earlier full run hit go's 10m default timeout under load average ~8; the rerun took 740s.
